source.text: אָ֚ז יִקְרָ֣א יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ לָרֽאוּבֵנִ֖י וְלַגָּדִ֑י וְלַחֲצִ֖י מַטֵּ֥ה מְנַשֶּֽׁה׃

records.literal_gloss: Then summoned Joshua the Reubenites and the Gadites and half [the] tribe of Manasseh.

en.L: Then Joshua summoned the Reubenites and the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
en.B: Then Joshua summoned the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
en.R: Then Joshua called together the tribes of Reuben and Gad and half of the tribe of Manasseh.

decisions.choice: the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh: the tribes that settled east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: These two and a half tribes had received land east of the Jordan from Moses on condition that their fighting men cross over and fight beside the other tribes until the whole land was taken (Numbers 32; Deuteronomy 3:12-20). Joshua held them to it before the crossing (1:12-18), and now that the land has been divided he releases them.

decisions.choice: then: at that time, when the land had been given and had rest
decisions.reason: "Then" ties the scene to the close of the land division (21:43-45), when the LORD had given Israel rest from its enemies. It marks the time in general terms; it does not say the scene followed the last chapter immediately.

decisions.choice: the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh (Balanced); the tribes of Reuben and Gad and half of the tribe of Manasseh (Readable)
decisions.reason: The three eastern groups are named many times in this chapter, in slightly different Hebrew forms ("the Reubenite", "the sons of Reuben"). Balanced and Readable name them in the same words every time, as 1:12 does, so the reader can follow them; Literal shows the Hebrew form.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם אַתֶּ֣ם שְׁמַרְתֶּ֔ם אֵ֚ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוָּ֣ה אֶתְכֶ֔ם מֹשֶׁ֖ה עֶ֣בֶד יְהוָ֑ה וַתִּשְׁמְע֣וּ בְקוֹלִ֔י לְכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־צִוִּ֖יתִי אֶתְכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to them, You, you have kept all that commanded you Moses [the] slave of Yahweh, and you have listened to my voice in all that I commanded you.

en.L: And he said to them, "You have kept all that Moses the slave of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded you, and you have listened to my voice in all that I commanded you.
en.B: He said to them, "You have carried out all that Moses the servant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded you, and in everything I have commanded you, you have obeyed me.
en.R: He said to them, "You have done everything Moses, the servant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, told you to do. And you have obeyed me in everything I told you to do.

decisions.choice: all that Moses commanded you: the terms of Numbers 32
decisions.reason: Moses had told these tribes to cross armed ahead of their fellow tribes and not return home until the land was won (Numbers 32:20-22; Deuteronomy 3:18-20). They had promised Joshua to obey him as they had obeyed Moses (1:16-17). Joshua now says that both promises have been kept.

decisions.choice: listened to my voice: obeyed me
decisions.reason: To listen to someone's voice is a common way of saying to obey (Genesis 22:18; Exodus 19:5).

decisions.choice: slave (Literal); servant (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 1:1, Moses' title follows the project's rule for this word: Literal keeps "slave", Balanced and Readable say "servant".

source.text: לֹֽא־עֲזַבְתֶּ֣ם אֶת־אֲחֵיכֶ֗ם זֶ֚ה יָמִ֣ים רַבִּ֔ים עַ֖ד הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה וּשְׁמַרְתֶּ֕ם אֶת־מִשְׁמֶ֕רֶת מִצְוַ֖ת יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Not you have forsaken your brothers these many days until this day, and you have kept the charge of [the] commandment of Yahweh your God.

en.L: You have not forsaken your brothers these many days, to this day, and you have kept the charge of the commandment of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.
en.B: All this long time, up to this very day, you have not abandoned your fellow Israelites. You have faithfully carried out the duty that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God commanded.
en.R: For a long time now, right up to today, you have not left the other tribes on their own. You have done the work {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God gave you to do.

decisions.choice: these many days: the long years of the wars of conquest
decisions.reason: The fighting took a long time (11:18). Caleb's words in 14:7 and 14:10 suggest about seven years from the spying of the land to the sharing out of it.

decisions.choice: the charge of the commandment: the duty entrusted to them by God's command
decisions.reason: The word for "charge" means something given into a person's keeping, a duty to be guarded and carried out (Genesis 26:5; Numbers 3:7). The duty here was to fight until the other tribes had their land.

decisions.choice: your fellow Israelites (Balanced); the other tribes (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Your brothers" means the other tribes of Israel, relatives as one people, not brothers in a family. Balanced and Readable say so.

source.text: וְעַתָּ֗ה הֵנִ֨יחַ יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶם֙ לַֽאֲחֵיכֶ֔ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּ֣ר לָהֶ֑ם וְעַתָּ֡ה פְּנוּ֩ וּלְכ֨וּ לָכֶ֜ם לְאָהֳלֵיכֶ֗ם אֶל־אֶ֨רֶץ֙ אֲחֻזַּתְכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר׀נָתַ֣ן לָכֶ֗ם מֹשֶׁה֙ עֶ֣בֶד יְהוָ֔ה בְּעֵ֖בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And now has given rest Yahweh your God to your brothers, as he spoke to them; and now turn and go for yourselves to your tents, to [the] land of your possession which gave to you Moses [the] slave of Yahweh across the Jordan.

en.L: And now {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has given rest to your brothers, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them. So now turn and go to your tents, to the land of your possession, which Moses the slave of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave you across the Jordan.
en.B: Now {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has given your fellow Israelites rest, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised them. So turn now and go home to your tents, to the land that is your own, which Moses the servant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave you on the other side of the Jordan.
en.R: Now {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has given the other tribes rest from their enemies, just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised. So now you may go back home to your own land. It is the land on the east side of the Jordan that Moses, the servant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, gave you.

decisions.choice: given rest: a settled life in the land, free from enemies
decisions.reason: Rest was the goal Moses set for the eastern tribes' service: they could go home when the LORD had given their brothers rest as he had given it to them (1:13-15; Deuteronomy 3:20). The narrator has just said that this has happened (21:44).

decisions.choice: go to your tents: go home
decisions.reason: "To your tents" is a set way of saying "home", used long after Israel lived in houses (Judges 7:8; 1 Kings 8:66).

decisions.choice: across the Jordan: here, east of it
decisions.reason: Joshua speaks at Shiloh, west of the river (verse 9), so the land "across the Jordan" is the land on its east side, given by Moses (Numbers 32:33).

decisions.choice: rest from their enemies; on the east side
decisions.reason: Readable says what the rest is and which side of the river is meant, both plain from the context (21:44; verse 9).

source.text: רַ֣ק׀שִׁמְר֣וּ מְאֹ֗ד לַעֲשׂ֨וֹת אֶת־הַמִּצְוָ֣ה וְאֶת־הַתּוֹרָה֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוָּ֣ה אֶתְכֶם֮ מֹשֶׁ֣ה עֶֽבֶד־יְהוָה֒ לְ֠אַהֲבָה אֶת־יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֜ם וְלָלֶ֧כֶת בְּכָל־דְּרָכָ֛יו וְלִשְׁמֹ֥ר מִצְוֺתָ֖יו וּלְדָבְקָה־ב֑וֹ וּלְעָבְד֕וֹ בְּכָל־לְבַבְכֶ֖ם וּבְכָל־נַפְשְׁכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Only take care very [much] to do the commandment and the law which commanded you Moses [the] slave of Yahweh, to love Yahweh your God and to walk in all his ways and to keep his commandments and to cling to him and to serve him with all your heart and with all your soul.

en.L: Only be very careful to do the commandment and the law that Moses the slave of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded you: to love {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, and to walk in all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ways, and to keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandments, and to cling to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and to serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with all your heart and with all your soul."
en.B: But take great care to carry out the commandment and the law which Moses the servant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} laid on you: love {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, walk in all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ways, keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandments, hold fast to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with all your heart and all your soul."
en.R: But be very careful to obey the commands and laws that Moses, the servant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, gave you. Love {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. Live the way {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wants you to live, and obey {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commands. Stay close to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with all your heart and with your whole self."

decisions.choice: the law: the whole of Moses' teaching, not only its rules
decisions.reason: The word means instruction or teaching. Joined with "the commandment", it sums up everything Moses taught Israel in the LORD's name (Deuteronomy 1:5; 4:44).

decisions.choice: love, walk, keep, cling, serve: the words of Deuteronomy
decisions.reason: Joshua's charge gathers the language of Moses' sermons (Deuteronomy 10:12; 11:13, 22; 13:5). The warriors leave with the heart of the law ringing in their ears, which makes the alarm over their altar in verses 11-20 all the sharper.

decisions.choice: cling to him: stay loyally joined to the LORD
decisions.reason: The verb is used of a husband joined to his wife (Genesis 2:24) and of Ruth clinging to Naomi (Ruth 1:14). It speaks of a close and loyal bond, not only of obeying rules (Deuteronomy 10:20; 23:8 of Joshua).

decisions.choice: soul: the whole living self
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word means life or self, the whole person who breathes and desires. "With all your soul" means with your whole being (Deuteronomy 6:5).

decisions.choice: Live the way he wants you to live; Stay close to him; your whole self
decisions.reason: Readable explains the pictures of walking in his ways and clinging to him, and says "your whole self" for "soul", as it does at Deuteronomy 10:12 and 11:22.

source.text: וַֽיְבָרְכֵ֖ם יְהוֹשֻׁ֑עַ וַֽיְשַׁלְּחֵ֔ם וַיֵּלְכ֖וּ אֶל־אָהֳלֵיהֶֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And blessed them Joshua and sent them away, and they went to their tents.

en.L: And Joshua blessed them and sent them away, and they went to their tents.
en.B: Then Joshua blessed them and sent them off, and they went home to their tents.
en.R: Then Joshua blessed them and sent them away, and they started for home.

decisions.choice: blessed them: asked God's good on them as they parted
decisions.reason: A leader's blessing at a parting or at the end of a great task is a prayer that God will do good to the people (Genesis 47:7; 2 Samuel 6:18; 1 Kings 8:55).

decisions.choice: they went: they set out; the story of the journey resumes in verse 9
decisions.reason: Verses 7-8 step back to add a note on Manasseh and Joshua's parting words; verse 9 then takes up the journey again.

decisions.choice: started for home
decisions.reason: Readable says "home" for "their tents" (see verse 4) and "started" because they reach the Jordan only in verse 10.

source.text: וְלַחֲצִ֣י׀שֵׁ֣בֶט הַֽמְנַשֶּׁ֗ה נָתַ֣ן מֹשֶׁה֮ בַּבָּשָׁן֒ וּלְחֶצְי֗וֹ נָתַ֤ן יְהוֹשֻׁ֨עַ֙ עִם־אֲחֵיהֶ֔ם בְּעֵ֥בֶרהַיַּרְדֵּ֖ן יָ֑מָּה וְ֠גַם כִּ֣י שִׁלְּחָ֧ם יְהוֹשֻׁ֛עַ אֶל־אָהֳלֵיהֶ֖ם וַיְבָרֲכֵֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And to half [the] tribe of the Manasseh had given Moses in the Bashan, and to its half gave Joshua with their brothers across the Jordan westward. And also when sent them Joshua to their tents, and he blessed them,

en.L: Now to [one] half of the tribe of Manasseh Moses had given [land] in Bashan, and to its [other] half Joshua had given [land] with their brothers across the Jordan to the west. And also, when Joshua sent them away to their tents, he blessed them,
en.B: Moses had given one half of the tribe of Manasseh land in Bashan; to the other half Joshua had given land west of the Jordan, beside their fellow Israelites. When Joshua sent the eastern tribes home, he blessed them
en.R: Moses had given land in Bashan to one half of the tribe of Manasseh. Joshua had given land to the other half of the tribe, west of the Jordan, next to the other tribes. When Joshua sent the eastern tribes home, he blessed them.

decisions.choice: the two halves of Manasseh: one east of the Jordan, one west
decisions.reason: Manasseh was split: Moses gave the clans of Machir land in Bashan and Gilead east of the river (13:29-31; Numbers 32:39-40), and Joshua gave the rest land west of it, beside Ephraim (17:1-13). The note explains why only half of Manasseh is going home.

decisions.choice: on the other side: the form the margin of the Hebrew text tells readers to read
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew text has "from the other side" here; the scribes' marginal note reads "on the other side", the usual phrase, which this translation follows. The place meant is the same either way.

decisions.choice: and also when Joshua sent them away: the narrator returns to the parting of verse 6
decisions.reason: After the note on Manasseh, the narrator goes back to Joshua's farewell to add what he said to the warriors as he blessed them (verse 8). "Them" are all the eastern warriors, Reuben and Gad with the eastern half of Manasseh.

decisions.choice: land; the eastern tribes
decisions.reason: The Hebrew leaves out what was given; Balanced and Readable say "land". They also say "the eastern tribes" for "them", since the last people named are the western half of Manasseh, who are not the ones being sent home.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם לֵאמֹ֗ר בִּנְכָסִ֨ים רַבִּ֜ים שׁ֤וּבוּ אֶל־אָֽהֳלֵיכֶם֙ וּבְמִקְנֶ֣ה רַב־מְאֹ֔ד בְּכֶ֨סֶף וּבְזָהָ֜ב וּבִנְחֹ֧שֶׁת וּבְבַרְזֶ֛ל וּבִשְׂלָמ֖וֹת הַרְבֵּ֣ה מְאֹ֑ד חִלְק֥וּ שְׁלַל־אֹיְבֵיכֶ֖ם עִם־אֲחֵיכֶֽם׃פ

records.literal_gloss: and he said to them, saying, With riches great return to your tents, and with livestock much very, with silver and with gold and with bronze and with iron and with garments many very; divide [the] spoil of your enemies with your brothers.

en.L: and said to them, "Return to your tents with great riches, and with very much livestock, with silver and with gold and with bronze and with iron and with very many garments. Divide the spoil of your enemies with your brothers."
en.B: and said to them, "Go back to your homes with great wealth: large herds of livestock, silver, gold, bronze and iron, and a great amount of clothing. Share the plunder taken from your enemies with your relatives at home."
en.R: He said to them, "Go back home. You are taking great wealth with you: many animals, silver, gold, bronze, iron, and lots of clothing. Share what you took from your enemies with your families and the rest of your people back home."

decisions.choice: with great riches: placed first for weight
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts "with great riches" before the verb "return", stressing the wealth they take home. The warriors who left their families to fight come back rich (compare 8:2, 27; 11:14).

decisions.choice: divide the spoil with your brothers: share it with those of their own tribes who stayed east
decisions.reason: Only the fighting men crossed; the families and many others stayed in Gilead (1:14; Numbers 32:26-27). The rule that those at home share the spoil with the warriors goes back to Numbers 31:27 and is kept by David (1 Samuel 30:24-25). "Your brothers" here are their own kin east of the river.

decisions.choice: your relatives at home (Balanced); your families and the rest of your people back home (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make plain that the "brothers" are the people of their own tribes waiting at home, not the western tribes (see m2).

source.text: וַיָּשֻׁ֣בוּ וַיֵּלְכ֡וּ בְּנֵי־רְאוּבֵ֨ן וּבְנֵי־גָ֜ד וַחֲצִ֣י׀שֵׁ֣בֶט הַֽמְנַשֶּׁ֗ה מֵאֵת֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מִשִּׁלֹ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּאֶֽרֶץ־כְּנָ֑עַן לָלֶ֜כֶת אֶל־אֶ֣רֶץ הַגִּלְעָ֗ד אֶל־אֶ֤רֶץ אֲחֻזָּתָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נֹֽאחֲזוּ־בָ֔הּ עַל־פִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה בְּיַד־מֹשֶֽׁה׃

records.literal_gloss: And returned and went [the] sons of Reuben and [the] sons of Gad and half [the] tribe of the Manasseh from with [the] sons of Israel from Shiloh which [is] in [the] land of Canaan, to go to [the] land of the Gilead, to [the] land of their possession which they had taken possession in it at [the] mouth of Yahweh by [the] hand of Moses.

en.L: So the sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh returned and went away from the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel at Shiloh, which [is] in the land of Canaan, to go to the land of Gilead, to the land of their possession, which they had taken possession of at the command of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} by the hand of Moses.
en.B: So the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh turned back and parted from the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} at Shiloh, in the land of Canaan, to go to the land of Gilead. That was their own land, which had become theirs at the command of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} given through Moses.
en.R: So the tribes of Reuben and Gad and half of the tribe of Manasseh left the other {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} at Shiloh, in Canaan. They headed home to the land of Gilead. It was their own land. They had received it because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded it through Moses.

decisions.choice: Shiloh: where the tent of meeting stood
decisions.reason: Israel had set up the tent of meeting at Shiloh, and the last lots for the land were cast there (18:1, 8-10; 19:51). The altar story turns on this: Shiloh is the place of the LORD's sanctuary (verses 19, 29).

decisions.choice: the land of Gilead: here the whole land of the eastern tribes
decisions.reason: Gilead is properly the hill country east of the Jordan between the Yarmuk and the Arnon valleys, but it can stand for all the land the two and a half tribes held there (Numbers 32:1, 29; Judges 20:1).

decisions.choice: at the mouth of the LORD by the hand of Moses: by the LORD's command, given through Moses
decisions.reason: "Mouth" stands for what someone says and "hand" for the person through whom something is done. The eastern land was theirs by God's own word through Moses (Numbers 32:28-33).

decisions.choice: the sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew "sons of". These are the tribes' warriors going home, so no gender setting is used. Balanced and Readable use the fixed names given at verse 1.

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ אֶל־גְּלִיל֣וֹת הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנָ֑עַן וַיִּבְנ֣וּ בְנֵי־רְאוּבֵ֣ן וּבְנֵי־גָ֡ד וַחֲצִ֣י שֵׁבֶט֩ הַֽמְנַשֶּׁ֨ה שָׁ֤ם מִזְבֵּ֨חַ֙ עַל־הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן מִזְבֵּ֥חַ גָּד֖וֹל לְמַרְאֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And they came to [the] districts of the Jordan which [is] in [the] land of Canaan, and built [the] sons of Reuben and [the] sons of Gad and half [the] tribe of the Manasseh there an altar by the Jordan, an altar great in appearance.

en.L: And they came to the districts of the Jordan that [are] in the land of Canaan, and the sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh built an altar there by the Jordan, an altar great to look at.
en.B: When they reached the region along the Jordan that lies in the land of Canaan, the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh built an altar there by the Jordan, an altar of imposing size.
en.R: When they came to the area by the Jordan River, on the Canaan side, the tribes of Reuben and Gad and half of the tribe of Manasseh built an altar there beside the river. It was very big and easy to see.

decisions.choice: the districts of the Jordan: the land along the river, perhaps a place called Geliloth
decisions.reason: The word means circles or districts. It may describe the land along the river here, or name a place, Geliloth, which 18:17 places near the border of Benjamin. The site of the altar cannot be fixed.

decisions.choice: in the land of Canaan: the altar stood west of the river
decisions.reason: "Canaan" here is the land west of the Jordan (verses 9, 32). So the tribes built the altar before they crossed back to their own land, on the side where the other tribes lived (see verse 11).

decisions.choice: great in appearance: large and meant to be seen
decisions.reason: The altar was built to be noticed. The builders explain why in verses 26-28: it was a copy of the LORD's altar, set up as a lasting witness, not for sacrifice.

decisions.choice: on the Canaan side
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly which bank of the river is meant, since "in the land of Canaan" means the west side here (m2).

source.text: וַיִּשְׁמְע֥וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר הִנֵּ֣ה בָנ֣וּ בְנֵֽי־רְאוּבֵ֣ן וּבְנֵי־גָ֡ד וַחֲצִי֩ שֵׁ֨בֶט הַֽמְנַשֶּׁ֜ה אֶת־הַמִּזְבֵּ֗חַ אֶל־מוּל֙ אֶ֣רֶץ כְּנַ֔עַן אֶל־גְּלִילוֹת֙ הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן אֶל־עֵ֖בֶר בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And heard [the] sons of Israel, saying, Look, have built [the] sons of Reuben and [the] sons of Gad and half [the] tribe of the Manasseh the altar at [the] front of [the] land of Canaan, in [the] districts of the Jordan, on [the] side of [the] sons of Israel.

en.L: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel heard [it] said, "Look, the sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh have built the altar at the frontier of the land of Canaan, in the districts of the Jordan, on the side belonging to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel."
en.B: Then the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} heard the report: "The Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh have built an altar at the edge of the land of Canaan, in the region along the Jordan, on the Israelite side."
en.R: Then the other {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} heard what had happened. People said, "The tribes of Reuben and Gad and half of the tribe of Manasseh have built an altar at the edge of Canaan. It is by the Jordan River, on our side of the river."

decisions.choice: at the frontier of Canaan, on the Israelites' side: on the west bank, at the edge of the land
alternatives: facing the land of Canaan, on the east bank
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean "facing the land of Canaan", which some take to put the altar on the east bank, looking across. But verse 10 says the altar was "in the land of Canaan", and "on the side of the sons of Israel" most naturally means the side where the other tribes lived. Read together, the report places it on the west bank at the border, where all Israel could see it.

decisions.choice: the altar: the one just described
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "the altar", pointing back to the great altar of verse 10.

decisions.choice: People said; on our side of the river
decisions.reason: Readable turns "heard, saying" into a report people passed on, and puts "the side of the sons of Israel" in the words of the Israelites who are speaking.

source.text: וַֽיִּשְׁמְע֖וּ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיִּקָּ֨הֲל֜וּ כָּל־עֲדַ֤ת בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ שִׁלֹ֔ה לַעֲל֥וֹת עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם לַצָּבָֽא׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And heard [the] sons of Israel, and assembled all [the] congregation of [the] sons of Israel [at] Shiloh to go up against them for war.

en.L: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel heard [it], and the whole congregation of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel gathered at Shiloh to go up against them to war.
en.B: When the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} heard this, the whole congregation of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} assembled at Shiloh to march out and fight against them.
en.R: When the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} heard about it, the whole community gathered at Shiloh. They were ready to go to war against the eastern tribes.

decisions.choice: to go up against them to war: the law's response to a rival altar
decisions.reason: The law allowed sacrifice only at the one place the LORD would choose (Deuteronomy 12:5-14; Leviticus 17:8-9), and it ordered war on any town in Israel that turned to other worship (Deuteronomy 13:13-19). The other tribes read the altar as that kind of rebellion (verses 16-19).

decisions.choice: at Shiloh: at the sanctuary
decisions.reason: They gather where the tent of meeting stands (18:1), the place that the new altar seemed to challenge.

decisions.choice: the eastern tribes
decisions.reason: Readable names the tribes meant by "them", since a new sentence begins.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלְח֨וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל אֶל־בְּנֵי־רְאוּבֵ֧ן וְאֶל־בְּנֵי־גָ֛ד וְאֶל־חֲצִ֥י שֵֽׁבֶט־מְנַשֶּׁ֖ה אֶל־אֶ֣רֶץ הַגִּלְעָ֑ד אֶת־פִּינְחָ֖ס בֶּן־אֶלְעָזָ֥ר הַכֹּהֵֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And sent [the] sons of Israel to [the] sons of Reuben and to [the] sons of Gad and to half [the] tribe of Manasseh, to [the] land of the Gilead, Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest.

en.L: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel sent to the sons of Reuben and to the sons of Gad and to the half-tribe of Manasseh, to the land of Gilead, Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest.
en.B: So the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} sent Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest to the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh in the land of Gilead.
en.R: So the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} sent Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest to the tribes of Reuben and Gad and half of the tribe of Manasseh in the land of Gilead.

decisions.choice: Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest: the priest known for his zeal at Peor
decisions.reason: Phinehas had acted against the sin at Peor and was given a covenant of lasting priesthood (Numbers 25:7-13); he also went with the army against Midian (Numbers 31:6). His father Eleazar was the chief priest (14:1; 21:1). Sending him shows how seriously the matter was taken, and Peor is the first thing the delegation mentions (verse 17).

decisions.choice: they sent: they ask before they fight
decisions.reason: Before striking, Israel sends to find out the truth, as the law required when a town was accused of turning away (Deuteronomy 13:15).

decisions.choice: sent Phinehas ... to
decisions.reason: The Hebrew names the people sent to before the man who was sent. Balanced and Readable put Phinehas first, the usual English order.

source.text: וַעֲשָׂרָ֤ה נְשִׂאִים֙ עִמּ֔וֹ נָשִׂ֨יא אֶחָ֜ד נָשִׂ֤יא אֶחָד֙ לְבֵ֣ית אָ֔ב לְכֹ֖ל מַטּ֣וֹת יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְאִ֨ישׁ רֹ֧אשׁ בֵּית־אֲבוֹתָ֛ם הֵ֖מָּה לְאַלְפֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: and ten leaders with him, leader one, leader one for [a] house of [a] father for all [the] tribes of Israel; and each head of [the] house of their fathers they [were] for [the] thousands of Israel.

en.L: And ten leaders [were] with him, one leader [for] each father's house for all the tribes of Israel; and each of them [was] the head of their fathers' house among the thousands of Israel.
en.B: With him went ten leaders, one leader from each ancestral family for every tribe of Israel. Each of them was the head of his family among the clans of Israel.
en.R: Ten leaders went with him, one from each of the tribes on the west side of the Jordan. Each man was the head of a family group among Israel's clans.

decisions.choice: a leader one, a leader one: one leader each
decisions.reason: Saying a phrase twice gives it a sense of "each" or "every": one leader for each ancestral house.

decisions.choice: ten leaders: one for each tribe west of the Jordan
decisions.reason: With Levi holding no tribal land and the two and a half eastern tribes on the other side, ten tribes remain west of the river (counting the western half of Manasseh). Here the "house of a father" seems to stand for a whole tribe, so the ten leaders speak for all of western Israel.

decisions.choice: the thousands of Israel: the large family groups, the clans
decisions.reason: As in Numbers 1:16, "thousands" names the clans into which the tribes were divided, not a count of a thousand people.

decisions.choice: one from each of the tribes on the west side of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Readable says which tribes the ten came from, using the count explained in m2.

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֜אוּ אֶל־בְּנֵי־רְאוּבֵ֧ן וְאֶל־בְּנֵי־גָ֛ד וְאֶל־חֲצִ֥י שֵֽׁבֶט־מְנַשֶּׁ֖ה אֶל־אֶ֣רֶץ הַגִּלְעָ֑ד וַיְדַבְּר֥וּ אִתָּ֖ם לֵאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And they came to [the] sons of Reuben and to [the] sons of Gad and to half [the] tribe of Manasseh, to [the] land of the Gilead, and they spoke with them, saying,

en.L: And they came to the sons of Reuben and to the sons of Gad and to the half-tribe of Manasseh, to the land of Gilead, and they spoke with them, saying,
en.B: They went to the land of Gilead, to the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh, and spoke with them:
en.R: They went to the tribes of Reuben and Gad and half of the tribe of Manasseh in the land of Gilead. They said to them,

decisions.choice: they came to the land of Gilead: the delegation crossed the river
decisions.reason: The altar was on the west bank (verses 10-11), but the delegation goes to the builders in their own land, east of the Jordan, to speak with them before any fighting (Deuteronomy 20:10).

source.text: כֹּ֣ה אָמְר֞וּ כֹּ֣ל׀עֲדַ֣ת יְהוָ֗ה מָֽה־הַמַּ֤עַל הַזֶּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֤ר מְעַלְתֶּם֙ בֵּאלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לָשׁ֣וּב הַיּ֔וֹם מֵאַחֲרֵ֖י יְהוָ֑ה בִּבְנֽוֹתְכֶ֤ם לָכֶם֙ מִזְבֵּ֔חַ לִמְרָדְכֶ֥ם הַיּ֖וֹם בַּיהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus say all [the] congregation of Yahweh: What [is] the breach of faith the this that you have committed against [the] God of Israel, to turn back this day from after Yahweh, by your building for yourselves an altar, by your rebelling this day against Yahweh?

en.L: "Thus says the whole congregation of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: 'What [is] this breach of faith that you have committed against the God of Israel, turning back this day from following {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} by building yourselves an altar, rebelling this day against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}?
en.B: "The whole congregation of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says this: 'How could you commit such a breach of faith against the God of Israel? Today you have turned away from following {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} by building yourselves an altar, rebelling against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} this very day.
en.R: "The whole community of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s people says this: 'How could you be so unfaithful to the God of Israel? Today you have turned away from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. You have built an altar for yourselves, and that is rebellion against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: breach of faith: a betrayal of trust against God
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for Achan's sin (7:1; verse 20): taking or doing what wrongs God, like a broken trust. The delegation repeats it in verses 20 and 22 and Phinehas in verse 31.

decisions.choice: building an altar is rebellion: sacrifice belonged at the LORD's one altar
decisions.reason: The law said Israel's offerings must be brought to the place the LORD chose, not offered at any altar (Leviticus 17:8-9; Deuteronomy 12:5-14). A second altar looked like a rival worship, and so a turning away from the LORD himself.

decisions.choice: turn back from after the LORD: stop following him
decisions.reason: To go "after" the LORD is to follow him as a people follow a leader; to turn back from after him is to give up following (Numbers 14:43; 32:15).

decisions.choice: the whole community of the LORD's people
decisions.reason: Readable explains "the congregation of the LORD" as the community of people who belong to him.

source.text: הַמְעַט־לָ֨נוּ֙ אֶת־עֲוֺ֣ן פְּע֔וֹר אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא־הִטַּהַ֨רְנוּ֙ מִמֶּ֔נּוּ עַ֖ד הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה וַיְהִ֥י הַנֶּ֖גֶף בַּעֲדַ֥ת יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: [Is it] too little for us, the iniquity of Peor, which not we have cleansed ourselves from it until this day, and came the plague on [the] congregation of Yahweh?

en.L: [Is] the iniquity of Peor too little for us, from which we have not cleansed ourselves to this day, though the plague came on the congregation of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}?
en.B: Was the sin at Peor not enough for us? To this day we have not cleansed ourselves from it, even though a plague struck the congregation of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Remember the sin at Peor! We are still not free of it, even today. Because of it a terrible sickness struck {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s people.

decisions.choice: the iniquity of Peor: Israel's worship of Baal of Peor
decisions.reason: In Moab, Israelite men joined the Moabites in sexual sin and in the worship of Baal of Peor, and a plague killed 24,000 people before Phinehas acted (Numbers 25:1-9; Deuteronomy 4:3).

decisions.choice: is it too little for us: a question that expects the answer no
decisions.reason: The question means: that sin was more than enough; must we add another?

decisions.choice: not cleansed to this day: the guilt of Peor still hung over Israel
decisions.reason: The speakers feel that Israel has not yet fully put that sin behind it, even though the plague was stopped. A new rebellion would add to an old guilt.

decisions.choice: Remember the sin at Peor!; a terrible sickness
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into a call to remember, which gives the same sense in plainer words, and explains "plague" as a deadly sickness.

source.text: וְאַתֶּם֙ תָּשֻׁ֣בוּ הַיּ֔וֹם מֵאַחֲרֵ֖י יְהוָ֑ה וְהָיָ֗ה אַתֶּ֞ם תִּמְרְד֤וּ הַיּוֹם֙ בַּֽיהוָ֔ה וּמָחָ֕ר אֶֽל־כָּל־עֲדַ֥ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל יִקְצֹֽף׃

records.literal_gloss: And you, you turn back this day from after Yahweh! And it will be, you rebel today against Yahweh, and tomorrow against all [the] congregation of Israel he will be angry.

en.L: And you, you are turning back this day from following {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! And it will be, [if] you rebel today against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, [then] tomorrow {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will be angry with the whole congregation of Israel.
en.B: And now you are turning away from following {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} today! If you rebel against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} today, tomorrow {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will be angry with the whole congregation of Israel.
en.R: And now today you are turning away from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! If you rebel against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} today, tomorrow {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will be angry with all the people of Israel.

decisions.choice: you rebel today ... tomorrow he will be angry: a condition and its result
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sets two clauses side by side, "today you rebel ... tomorrow he will be angry", so that the first states the condition and the second what follows from it.

decisions.choice: angry with the whole congregation: one group's sin brings judgment on all
decisions.reason: Israel stands before God as one people, so the sin of some puts all at risk, as Achan's did (7:1, 11-12; verse 20).

decisions.choice: [if] ... [then]
decisions.reason: Literal brackets the words that show the condition, which the Hebrew leaves to the setting of the clauses.

source.text: וְאַ֨ךְ אִם־טְמֵאָ֜ה אֶ֣רֶץ אֲחֻזַּתְכֶ֗ם עִבְר֨וּ לָכֶ֜ם אֶל־אֶ֨רֶץ אֲחֻזַּ֤ת יְהוָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֤ר שָֽׁכַן־שָׁם֙ מִשְׁכַּ֣ן יְהוָ֔ה וְהֵאָחֲז֖וּ בְּתוֹכֵ֑נוּ וּבַֽיהוָ֣ה אַל־תִּמְרֹ֗דוּ וְאֹתָ֨נוּ֙ אֶל־תִּמְרֹ֔דוּ בִּבְנֹֽתְכֶ֤ם לָכֶם֙ מִזְבֵּ֔חַ מִֽבַּלְעֲדֵ֔י מִזְבַּ֖ח יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: But surely if unclean [is the] land of your possession, cross over for yourselves to [the] land of [the] possession of Yahweh, where dwells there [the] tabernacle of Yahweh, and take possession among us; but against Yahweh do not rebel, and us do not rebel against, by your building for yourselves an altar besides [the] altar of Yahweh our God.

en.L: But if the land of your possession is unclean, cross over to the land of the possession of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, where the tabernacle of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} dwells, and take possession among us. But do not rebel against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and do not rebel against us, by building yourselves an altar besides the altar of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God.
en.B: But if the land you possess is unclean, come over to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s own land, where {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s tabernacle stands, and take a share of land among us. Only do not rebel against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and do not rebel against us, by building an altar for yourselves other than the altar of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God.
en.R: If your land is unclean, then come across the river into {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s land, where {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} tabernacle is. Take land among us. Only do not rebel against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} or against us. Do not build another altar for yourselves besides the altar of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God.

decisions.choice: if your land is unclean: if the land east of the Jordan is not fit for the LORD's worship
decisions.reason: The speakers allow that the eastern tribes may feel cut off from the LORD in a land without his sanctuary. The promised land proper ran to the Jordan (Numbers 34:12), and the LORD's land is the land where his tabernacle stands. If that is the fear, the answer is to move west, not to build a new altar.

decisions.choice: where the tabernacle dwells: where the LORD's dwelling-tent stands
decisions.reason: The verb "dwell" and the word "tabernacle" come from the same root. The tent is the place where the LORD lives among his people (Exodus 25:8-9), now at Shiloh (18:1).

decisions.choice: do not rebel against us: do not set yourselves against the rest of Israel
decisions.reason: The Hebrew joins "rebel" with "us" in an unusual way. It may mean rebelling against the other tribes, or making them share the guilt of rebellion ("do not make rebels of us"), which fits verses 18 and 20. Either way the speakers fear the altar will divide Israel.

decisions.choice: the land you possess / your land; take a share of land among us / take land among us
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use plain words for the repeated "possession" and "take possession", which in Literal keep the Hebrew wordplay.

source.text: הֲל֣וֹא׀עָכָ֣ן בֶּן־זֶ֗רַח מָ֤עַל מַ֨עַל֙ בַּחֵ֔רֶם וְעַֽל־כָּל־עֲדַ֥ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל הָ֣יָה קָ֑צֶף וְהוּא֙ אִ֣ישׁ אֶחָ֔ד לֹ֥א גָוַ֖ע בַּעֲוֺנֽוֹ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Not Achan son of Zerah did commit a breach of faith in the devoted things, and on all [the] congregation of Israel was wrath? And he [was] one man; not he perished alone in his iniquity.

en.L: Did not Achan son of Zerah commit a breach of faith in the devoted things, and wrath came on the whole congregation of Israel? And he [was] one man; he did not perish [alone] in his iniquity.'"
en.B: When Achan son of Zerah broke faith over the devoted things, did not wrath fall on the whole congregation of Israel? He was only one man, but he was not the only one to die for his sin.'"
en.R: Remember Achan son of Zerah. He was unfaithful when he took some of the devoted things, the things that belonged to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} alone. Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was angry with the whole community of Israel. Achan was only one man, but he was not the only one who died because of his sin.'"

decisions.choice: Achan: the man who took from the devoted things of Jericho
decisions.reason: Achan kept for himself goods from Jericho that were given over wholly to the LORD. Because of him Israel was defeated at Ai, thirty-six men died there, and his family died with him (7:1, 5, 24-26).

decisions.choice: he did not perish alone: his one sin cost other lives too
alternatives: He was one man; did he not die for his sin?
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is short: "and he one man; he did not perish in his iniquity." The sense is that although he was only one man, he did not die alone; others died with him and because of him. Another way to take it is as a question, "Though he was one man, did he not die for his sin?", which stresses that sin was punished. The first fits the speakers' point, that one person's sin falls on the whole people.

decisions.choice: son of Zerah: a descendant of Zerah
decisions.reason: Achan's line was "son of Carmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah" (7:1, 18). Here only the clan's founder is named.

decisions.choice: the things that belonged to the LORD alone; the LORD was angry
decisions.reason: Readable explains "devoted things" as in 7:1 and says whose wrath is meant, which the Hebrew leaves unsaid but 7:1 states.

source.text: וַֽיַּעֲנוּ֙ בְּנֵי־רְאוּבֵ֣ן וּבְנֵי־גָ֔ד וַחֲצִ֖י שֵׁ֣בֶט הַֽמְנַשֶּׁ֑ה וַֽיְדַבְּר֔וּ אֶת־רָאשֵׁ֖י אַלְפֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And answered [the] sons of Reuben and [the] sons of Gad and half [the] tribe of the Manasseh and spoke with [the] heads of [the] thousands of Israel:

en.L: And the sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh answered, and they spoke with the heads of the thousands of Israel,
en.B: Then the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh answered the heads of the clans of Israel:
en.R: Then the tribes of Reuben and Gad and half of the tribe of Manasseh answered the leaders of Israel's clans. They said,

decisions.choice: the heads of the thousands of Israel: the ten clan leaders
decisions.reason: These are the ten leaders who came with Phinehas (verse 14); "thousands" means clans, as there.

source.text: אֵל֩׀אֱלֹהִ֨ים׀יְהוָ֜ה אֵ֣ל׀אֱלֹהִ֤ים׀יְהוָה֙ ה֣וּא יֹדֵ֔עַ וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל ה֣וּא יֵדָ֑ע אִם־בְּמֶ֤רֶד וְאִם־בְּמַ֨עַל֙ בַּֽיהוָ֔ה אַל־תּוֹשִׁיעֵ֖נוּ הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: El, God, Yahweh! El, God, Yahweh! He knows, and Israel, it shall know! If in rebellion and if in breach of faith against Yahweh, do not save us this day,

en.L: "[The] Mighty One, God, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! [The] Mighty One, God, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! He knows, and Israel, let it know! If [it was] in rebellion, or if in breach of faith against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, do not save us this day,
en.B: "The Mighty One, God, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! The Mighty One, God, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! He knows, and let Israel know too! If this was rebellion or a breach of faith against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, do not spare us today,
en.R: "The Mighty One, God, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! The Mighty One, God, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! He knows the truth, and we want Israel to know it too. If we have rebelled against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} or been unfaithful to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, then do not spare our lives today.

decisions.choice: El, Elohim, YHWH: three names of God called out together, and called out twice
alternatives: The God of gods, the LORD!
The LORD is God of gods!
decisions.reason: The tribes open their answer by crying out three names of God in a row: El, "the Mighty One", the old word for God; Elohim, "God"; and the LORD's own name. The same three open Psalm 50:1. Saying them twice makes a solemn oath: they call the God of Israel by every name to witness that they are telling the truth. The words can also be read as one title, "the God of gods, the LORD", as in Deuteronomy 10:17, or as a statement, "the LORD is God of gods". But the Hebrew here has no "of" between the first two words, as Deuteronomy 10:17 does, so this translation reads three names side by side.

decisions.choice: he knows, and Israel shall know: God is called as witness, and Israel will see the truth
decisions.reason: The tribes appeal first to God, who sees the heart, and then to Israel, who will come to know that their purpose was innocent (verses 24-28).

decisions.choice: do not save us today: a curse the speakers call down on themselves
alternatives: addressed to the delegation: do not spare us
decisions.reason: Inside the oath the speakers break off to say: if we are guilty, let no one rescue us. The words are most likely addressed to God, as part of the oath; they may also be addressed to the Israelites, meaning "then do not spare us". The sense is the same: if the charge is true, they deserve the punishment.

decisions.choice: if ... if ...: the oath continues into verse 23
decisions.reason: The "if" clauses run on into verse 23 and end with "may the LORD himself require it". That is the form of an oath: if we did this, may God punish us.

decisions.choice: The Mighty One, God, the LORD!
decisions.reason: Each level keeps three names, with "the Mighty One" for El so that it can be told apart from "God" for Elohim, as at Psalm 50:1. Readable keeps the same cry; it is short and plain enough.

source.text: לִבְנ֥וֹת לָ֨נוּ֙ מִזְבֵּ֔חַ לָשׁ֖וּב מֵאַחֲרֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְאִם־לְהַעֲל֨וֹת עָלָ֜יו עוֹלָ֣ה וּמִנְחָ֗ה וְאִם־לַעֲשׂ֤וֹת עָלָיו֙ זִבְחֵ֣י שְׁלָמִ֔ים יְהוָ֖ה ה֥וּא יְבַקֵּֽשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: to build for ourselves an altar to turn back from after Yahweh; and if to offer up on it burnt offering and grain offering, and if to make on it sacrifices of peace offerings, Yahweh, he, may he require [it].

en.L: to build ourselves an altar to turn back from following {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; and if [it was] to offer on it burnt offering and grain offering, or if to make on it sacrifices of peace offerings, may {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} require [it].
en.B: if we built ourselves an altar to turn away from following {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, or to offer burnt offerings and grain offerings on it, or to present peace offerings on it, may {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} call us to account.
en.R: If we built this altar to turn away from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, or to offer burnt offerings or grain offerings or peace offerings on it, may {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} punish us.

decisions.choice: burnt offering, grain offering, peace offerings: the sacrifices of the sanctuary
decisions.reason: These are the main offerings of the law: the burnt offering wholly burned (Leviticus 1), the grain offering (Leviticus 2) and the peace offerings shared in a meal (Leviticus 3). The tribes deny that their altar is for any of them.

decisions.choice: may the LORD himself require it: may God himself call us to account
decisions.reason: To "require" something from someone is to demand that they answer for it, often for blood or a broken oath (Deuteronomy 18:19; 1 Samuel 20:16). "Himself" stresses that God will be the judge.

decisions.choice: punish us
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of "require", which Balanced keeps as "call us to account".

source.text: וְאִם־לֹ֤א מִדְּאָגָה֙ מִדָּבָ֔ר עָשִׂ֥ינוּ אֶת־זֹ֖את לֵאמֹ֑ר מָחָ֗ר יֹאמְר֨וּ בְנֵיכֶ֤ם לְבָנֵ֨ינוּ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר מַה־לָּכֶ֕ם וְלַֽיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And if not from anxiety, from [a] matter we have done this, saying, Tomorrow will say your sons to our sons, saying, What to you and to Yahweh, [the] God of Israel?

en.L: No, out of anxiety, for a reason we have done this, thinking that tomorrow your {{gender:children|sons}} might say to our {{gender:children|sons}}, 'What [is there] to you and to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel?
en.B: No, we did it because we were worried about what might happen. We thought that someday your descendants might say to ours, 'What do you have to do with {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel?
en.R: No! We did it because we were afraid of what might happen later. We thought that someday your descendants might say to our descendants, 'What right do you have to worship {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel?

decisions.choice: and if not: "no, truly", the turn from denial to the real reason
decisions.reason: In an oath "if not" means "surely" or "on the contrary". Having sworn what the altar is not for, they now say what it is for.

decisions.choice: from anxiety, from a matter: out of worry over a real concern
decisions.reason: The tribes acted from fear of something that could happen, explained in the rest of verses 24-25.

decisions.choice: tomorrow: in time to come
decisions.reason: "Tomorrow" often means the future, when children ask their parents what things mean (Exodus 13:14; Deuteronomy 6:20; 4:6 of the Jordan stones).

decisions.choice: what to you and to the LORD: you have no part with the LORD
decisions.reason: "What to me and to you?" is a way of saying two parties have nothing in common (Judges 11:12; 2 Samuel 16:10). The fear is that the western tribes would deny the eastern ones any share in Israel's God.

decisions.choice: your children/sons ... our children/sons (Literal); your descendants ... ours (Balanced)
decisions.reason: The "sons" are the future generations of both groups, men and women, so Literal uses the gender setting and Balanced says "descendants".

decisions.choice: What right do you have to worship the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the question's point, which verse 25 confirms: that the eastern tribes might be refused a place in the LORD's worship.

source.text: וּגְב֣וּל נָֽתַן־יְ֠הוָה בֵּינֵ֨נוּ וּבֵינֵיכֶ֜ם בְּנֵי־רְאוּבֵ֤ן וּבְנֵי־גָד֙ אֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן אֵין־לָכֶ֥ם חֵ֖לֶק בַּֽיהוָ֑ה וְהִשְׁבִּ֤יתוּ בְנֵיכֶם֙ אֶת־בָּנֵ֔ינוּ לְבִלְתִּ֖י יְרֹ֥א אֶת־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And [a] border has put Yahweh between us and between you, [the] sons of Reuben and [the] sons of Gad, the Jordan; not to you [is] [a] portion in Yahweh. And will make cease your sons our sons from fearing Yahweh.

en.L: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has put a border between us and you, sons of Reuben and sons of Gad: the Jordan. [There is] no portion for you in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.' So your {{gender:children|sons}} would make our {{gender:children|sons}} cease to fear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has set the Jordan as a border between us and you, you Reubenites and Gadites. You have no share in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.' In that way your descendants could make ours stop fearing {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} made the Jordan River a border between us and you people of Reuben and Gad. You have no share in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.' If that happened, your descendants might make our descendants stop worshiping {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: sons of Reuben and sons of Gad: the future westerners' words to the eastern tribes
decisions.reason: In the imagined words the western descendants address the people of Reuben and Gad. Half of Manasseh is not named here, nor in verses 32-34; Reuben and Gad stand for the whole eastern group, perhaps because Manasseh also had land west of the river.

decisions.choice: a portion in the LORD: a share in belonging to the LORD and in his worship
decisions.reason: A "portion" is a share of an inheritance. To have a portion in the LORD is to belong to his people and to share in his worship; the Levites had the LORD as their portion (Deuteronomy 10:9; 18:1-2).

decisions.choice: fearing the LORD: honoring and worshiping him
decisions.reason: The fear of the LORD is reverence shown in worship and obedience (Deuteronomy 6:2, 13). Cut off from the sanctuary, later generations might stop worshiping him.

decisions.choice: you Reubenites and Gadites (Balanced); you people of Reuben and Gad (Readable)
decisions.reason: Only two tribes are named here, so Balanced and Readable name only those two, in the forms used elsewhere in the chapter.

decisions.choice: stop worshiping the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of "fearing" here, which is worship rather than terror (m3).

source.text: וַנֹּ֕אמֶר נַעֲשֶׂה־נָּ֣א לָ֔נוּ לִבְנ֖וֹת אֶת־הַמִּזְבֵּ֑חַ לֹ֥א לְעוֹלָ֖ה וְלֹ֥א לְזָֽבַח׃

records.literal_gloss: And we said, Let us do, please, for ourselves, to build the altar, not for burnt offering and not for sacrifice,

en.L: And we said, 'Let us now act for ourselves to build the altar, not for burnt offering and not for sacrifice,
en.B: So we said, 'Let us take action and build an altar, not for burnt offerings or for sacrifices,
en.R: So we said, 'Let us build an altar. It will not be for burnt offerings or other sacrifices.

decisions.choice: let us act to build: let us take steps and build
decisions.reason: The speakers report their own decision: "let us do" joined to "to build" means let us set about building.

decisions.choice: not for burnt offering and not for sacrifice: an altar that would never be used
decisions.reason: They knew the law allowed only one altar for sacrifice (Deuteronomy 12:13-14), so they built theirs to stand as a sign and not to be used (verses 27-29).

source.text: כִּי֩ עֵ֨ד ה֜וּא בֵּינֵ֣ינוּ וּבֵינֵיכֶ֗ם וּבֵ֣ין דֹּרוֹתֵינוּ֮ אַחֲרֵינוּ֒ לַעֲבֹ֞ד אֶת־עֲבֹדַ֤ת יְהוָה֙ לְפָנָ֔יו בְּעֹלוֹתֵ֥ינוּ וּבִזְבָחֵ֖ינוּ וּבִשְׁלָמֵ֑ינוּ וְלֹא־יֹאמְר֨וּ בְנֵיכֶ֤ם מָחָר֙ לְבָנֵ֔ינוּ אֵין־לָכֶ֥ם חֵ֖לֶק בַּיהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: but [a] witness it [is] between us and between you and between our generations after us, to serve [the] service of Yahweh before him with our burnt offerings and with our sacrifices and with our peace offerings; and not will say your sons tomorrow to our sons, Not to you [is] [a] portion in Yahweh.

en.L: but it [is] a witness between us and you and between our generations after us, that we will do the service of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with our burnt offerings and with our sacrifices and with our peace offerings; and [so that] your {{gender:children|sons}} will not say tomorrow to our {{gender:children|sons}}, "[There is] no portion for you in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."'
en.B: but to be a witness between us and you, and between the generations after us, that we are to worship {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} presence by bringing our burnt offerings, sacrifices and peace offerings. So your descendants will never be able to say to ours in days to come, "You have no share in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."'
en.R: It will be a witness between you and us, and between our children and grandchildren after us. It will show that we will worship {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy tent. We will bring our burnt offerings, sacrifices and peace offerings there. Then later on your descendants will not be able to tell ours, "You have no share in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."'

decisions.choice: a witness: a lasting sign that proves something
decisions.reason: A heap of stones could be a witness to an agreement (Genesis 31:44-52), and the stones from the Jordan were a sign for later generations (4:6-7). The altar is to prove that the eastern tribes belong to the LORD's people.

decisions.choice: to serve the service of the LORD before him: to worship at his sanctuary
decisions.reason: "Before him" means in the LORD's presence, at the tabernacle where his altar stands (verse 29). The tribes mean to bring their offerings there, not to their own altar.

decisions.choice: between our generations after us: the later generations of both sides
decisions.reason: "Our generations" here takes in the descendants on both sides of the river, as the rest of the verse shows.

decisions.choice: at his holy tent
decisions.reason: Readable says where "before him" is: at the tabernacle, as verse 29 says.

source.text: וַנֹּ֕אמֶר וְהָיָ֗ה כִּֽי־יֹאמְר֥וּ אֵלֵ֛ינוּ וְאֶל־דֹּרֹתֵ֖ינוּ מָחָ֑ר וְאָמַ֡רְנוּ רְא֣וּ אֶת־תַּבְנִית֩ מִזְבַּ֨ח יְהוָ֜ה אֲשֶׁר־עָשׂ֣וּ אֲבוֹתֵ֗ינוּ לֹ֤א לְעוֹלָה֙ וְלֹ֣א לְזֶ֔בַח כִּי־עֵ֣ד ה֔וּא בֵּינֵ֖ינוּ וּבֵינֵיכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And we said, And it will be when they say to us and to our generations tomorrow, and we will say, See [the] copy of [the] altar of Yahweh which made our fathers, not for burnt offering and not for sacrifice, but [a] witness it [is] between us and between you.

en.L: And we said, 'And it will be, if they say [this] to us or to our generations tomorrow, then we will say, "See the copy of the altar of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that our fathers made, not for burnt offering and not for sacrifice, but it [is] a witness between us and you."'
en.B: We said, 'If that is ever said to us or to our descendants, our answer will be, "Look at this copy of the altar of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, which our ancestors made. It is not for burnt offerings or sacrifices. It is a witness between us and you."'
en.R: We said, 'If they ever say that to us or to our children in the future, we will answer, "Look! Our ancestors made this altar to look like the altar of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. It is not for burnt offerings or sacrifices. It is a witness between us and you."'

decisions.choice: copy: a model made after a pattern
decisions.reason: The word is used of the pattern for the tabernacle that Moses was shown (Exodus 25:9, 40). The altar was a likeness of the LORD's altar, and so pointed to it.

decisions.choice: our fathers: the builders, seen from the later generations
decisions.reason: The words are what the eastern tribes' descendants will say, so "our fathers" are the people now speaking.

decisions.choice: our ancestors
decisions.reason: "Fathers" here means the generation before, so Balanced and Readable say "ancestors".

source.text: חָלִילָה֩ לָּ֨נוּ מִמֶּ֜נּוּ לִמְרֹ֣ד בַּֽיהוָ֗ה וְלָשׁ֤וּב הַיּוֹם֙ מֵאַחֲרֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה לִבְנ֣וֹת מִזְבֵּ֔חַ לְעֹלָ֖ה לְמִנְחָ֣ה וּלְזָ֑בַח מִלְּבַ֗ד מִזְבַּח֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ אֲשֶׁ֖ר לִפְנֵ֥י מִשְׁכָּנֽוֹ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Far be it for us from us to rebel against Yahweh and to turn back this day from after Yahweh, to build [an] altar for burnt offering, for grain offering, and for sacrifice, besides [the] altar of Yahweh our God which [is] before his tabernacle.

en.L: Far be it from us to rebel against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and to turn back this day from following {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} by building an altar for burnt offering, for grain offering, and for sacrifice, besides the altar of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God that [is] before {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} tabernacle."
en.B: Far be it from us to rebel against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and to stop following {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} today by building an altar for burnt offerings, grain offerings or sacrifices apart from the altar of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God that stands in front of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} tabernacle."
en.R: We would never rebel against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} or turn away from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} now. We would never build an altar for burnt offerings, grain offerings or sacrifices besides the altar of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God, which stands in front of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} tabernacle."

decisions.choice: far be it from us: a strong denial
decisions.reason: The word means something like "it would be unthinkable, a profane thing" (Genesis 18:25; 44:7). The tribes reject the charge outright.

decisions.choice: the altar before his tabernacle: the bronze altar at the entrance of the tent at Shiloh
decisions.reason: The altar of burnt offering stood in front of the tabernacle's entrance (Exodus 40:6, 29). It was Israel's one altar for sacrifice.

decisions.choice: We would never
decisions.reason: Readable says the strong denial in plain words and repeats it for the second clause.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֞ע פִּֽינְחָ֣ס הַכֹּהֵ֗ן וּנְשִׂיאֵ֨י הָעֵדָ֜ה וְרָאשֵׁ֨י אַלְפֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתּ֔וֹ אֶת־הַ֨דְּבָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֧ר דִּבְּר֛וּ בְּנֵי־רְאוּבֵ֥ן וּבְנֵי־גָ֖ד וּבְנֵ֣י מְנַשֶּׁ֑ה וַיִּיטַ֖ב בְּעֵינֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And heard Phinehas the priest and [the] leaders of the congregation and [the] heads of [the] thousands of Israel who [were] with him the words that spoke [the] sons of Reuben and [the] sons of Gad and [the] sons of Manasseh, and it was good in their eyes.

en.L: And Phinehas the priest and the leaders of the congregation and the heads of the thousands of Israel who [were] with him heard the words that the sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad and the sons of Manasseh spoke, and it was good in their eyes.
en.B: When Phinehas the priest and the leaders of the congregation, the heads of the clans of Israel who were with him, heard what the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh said, they were satisfied.
en.R: Phinehas the priest and the leaders of the community, the heads of Israel's clans who were with him, listened to what the tribes of Reuben and Gad and half of the tribe of Manasseh said. They were pleased with it.

decisions.choice: the leaders of the congregation and the heads of the thousands: the same ten men
decisions.reason: These are the ten leaders of verse 14, each the head of a family among Israel's clans. The two titles describe one group.

decisions.choice: the sons of Manasseh: the eastern half of Manasseh
decisions.reason: Here and in verse 31 the Hebrew says simply "the sons of Manasseh", but it means the same group called the half-tribe of Manasseh elsewhere in the chapter.

decisions.choice: it was good in their eyes: they were satisfied
decisions.reason: "Good in the eyes of" means approved of or pleasing to someone.

decisions.choice: the half-tribe of Manasseh / half of the tribe of Manasseh
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep the fixed name of the group used throughout the chapter (m2); Literal keeps "the sons of Manasseh".

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר פִּֽינְחָ֣ס בֶּן־אֶלְעָזָ֣ר הַכֹּהֵ֡ן אֶל־בְּנֵי־רְאוּבֵ֨ן וְאֶל־בְּנֵי־גָ֜ד וְאֶל־בְּנֵ֣י מְנַשֶּׁ֗ה הַיּ֤וֹם׀יָדַ֨עְנוּ֙ כִּֽי־בְתוֹכֵ֣נוּ יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹֽא־מְעַלְתֶּ֥ם בַּֽיהוָ֖ה הַמַּ֣עַל הַזֶּ֑ה אָ֗ז הִצַּלְתֶּ֛ם אֶת־בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מִיַּ֥ד יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest to [the] sons of Reuben and to [the] sons of Gad and to [the] sons of Manasseh, Today we know that among us [is] Yahweh, that not you have committed against Yahweh the breach of faith the this; then you have delivered [the] sons of Israel from [the] hand of Yahweh.

en.L: And Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest said to the sons of Reuben and to the sons of Gad and to the sons of Manasseh, "Today we know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] among us, because you have not committed this breach of faith against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Now you have delivered the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel from the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."
en.B: Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest said to the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh, "Today we know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is in our midst, since you have not broken faith with {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in this way. By this you have rescued the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} from the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."
en.R: Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest said to the tribes of Reuben and Gad and half of the tribe of Manasseh, "Now we know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is with us. You have not been unfaithful to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in this way. So you have saved the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} from being punished by {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

decisions.choice: the LORD is among us: he is still present with his people and has not turned against them
decisions.reason: A sin like Achan's had made the LORD withdraw his help (7:11-12). Learning that no such sin has been committed, Phinehas sees that the LORD is still with Israel.

decisions.choice: then: in that case, as a result
decisions.reason: The word usually means "then" in time; here it draws the result: since you have not sinned, you have spared Israel.

decisions.choice: from the hand of the LORD: from the LORD's punishment
decisions.reason: The "hand" of the LORD here is his power to judge, the anger the delegation feared would fall on all Israel (verses 18, 20).

decisions.choice: from being punished by the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of the LORD's hand (m3).

records.literal_gloss: And returned Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest and the leaders from with [the] sons of Reuben and from with [the] sons of Gad, from [the] land of the Gilead, to [the] land of Canaan, to [the] sons of Israel, and they brought back to them word.

en.L: And Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest and the leaders returned from the sons of Reuben and from the sons of Gad, from the land of Gilead to the land of Canaan, to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, and brought them back word.
en.B: Then Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest and the leaders left the Reubenites and the Gadites in the land of Gilead and returned to the land of Canaan, to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, and gave them their report.
en.R: Then Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest and the leaders left the tribes of Reuben and Gad in Gilead. They went back to Canaan and told the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} what had happened.

decisions.choice: the sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad: the whole eastern group
decisions.reason: As in verse 25, only Reuben and Gad are named, but the eastern half of Manasseh is meant as well (verses 30-31).

decisions.choice: brought back word: reported
decisions.reason: To bring back word is to give the report of a mission (13:3 of spies, Numbers 13:26).

source.text: וַיִּיטַ֣ב הַדָּבָ֗ר בְּעֵינֵי֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיְבָרֲכ֥וּ אֱלֹהִ֖ים בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְלֹ֣א אָמְר֗וּ לַעֲל֤וֹת עֲלֵיהֶם֙ לַצָּבָ֔א לְשַׁחֵת֙ אֶת־הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֛ר בְּנֵי־רְאוּבֵ֥ן וּבְנֵי־גָ֖ד יֹשְׁבִ֥ים בָּֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And was good the word in [the] eyes of [the] sons of Israel, and blessed God [the] sons of Israel, and not they said to go up against them for war, to destroy the land which [the] sons of Reuben and [the] sons of Gad [were] living in it.

en.L: And the word was good in the eyes of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, and the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel blessed God, and they spoke no more of going up against them to war, to destroy the land where the sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad were living.
en.B: The report pleased the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, and they praised God. They did not speak again of going to war against them to lay waste the land where the Reubenites and the Gadites lived.
en.R: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} were pleased with the report, and they praised God. They stopped talking about going to war against the tribes of Reuben and Gad and destroying the land where they lived.

decisions.choice: blessed God: praised and thanked God
decisions.reason: When people bless God, they speak well of him and thank him, as Abraham's servant did when his prayer was answered (Genesis 24:48; Deuteronomy 8:10).

decisions.choice: they did not say to go up: they dropped the plan for war
decisions.reason: "Did not say" means they no longer spoke of it; the threat of verse 12 was set aside.

decisions.choice: praised God
decisions.reason: With God as the one blessed, Balanced and Readable say "praised", since in English blessing usually passes from a greater to a lesser.

records.literal_gloss: And called [the] sons of Reuben and [the] sons of Gad the altar: For [a] witness it [is] between us that Yahweh [is] the God.

en.L: And the sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad named the altar [Witness]: "For it [is] a witness between us that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] God."
en.B: The Reubenites and the Gadites named the altar Witness, "because," they said, "it stands as a witness between us that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is God."
en.R: The tribes of Reuben and Gad named the altar Witness. They said, "This altar is a witness between us that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is God."

decisions.choice: the name Witness is understood: the Hebrew gives the reason but not the name itself
alternatives: named the altar: 'It is a witness between us that the LORD is God'
decisions.reason: The standard Hebrew text says "they called the altar, for it is a witness ..." and gives no name. A few Hebrew manuscripts and the Syriac version have the name "Ed", "Witness", and the reason that follows, built on the same word, suggests it. Others take the whole saying as the name, or read "they called the altar so". This translation supplies "Witness", in brackets at Literal.

decisions.choice: the LORD is God: he alone is the true God
decisions.reason: With the article, the Hebrew says the LORD is "the God", the one true God, as in Deuteronomy 4:35, 39 and 1 Kings 18:39. The altar witnesses that both sides of the river worship him.

decisions.choice: [Witness]
decisions.reason: Literal brackets the name, which the Hebrew does not write (m1).
